initial_observation.demographics: Caucasian male patient diagnosed in his 70s; has a monozygotic twin brother
initial_observation.encounter_context: initial diagnostic workup for diffuse symptoms including musculoskeletal complaints and pigmentations over several decades
initial_observation.chief_complaint: early-onset arthropathy, tendinopathy, osteopenia, visible discolouration of the auricular regions and fingers, discolouration of the sclera, secondary glaucoma, proteinuria, calcification of the mitral valve, black urethral and prostate stones
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: Patient presented with multisystemic symptoms evolving over decades, including pigmentations noticed since early age but undiagnosed, progressive musculoskeletal symptoms starting with knee problems in his 50s, proteinuria detected incidentally in early 50s, and eosinophils detected in blood suggesting eosinophilic asthma in late 40s. Initial ophthalmologic evaluation revealed scleral pigmentation without further diagnosis. Numerous prior investigations and hospital admissions occurred before final diagnosis was made in early 70s after black discolouration in bone tissue was intraoperatively observed in the twin brother.
presenting_symptoms: visible discolouration of auricular regions and fingers
known_prior_history: small black spots on underpants and bed sheets since young age
use of continuous positive airway pressure for sleep apnoea
no urinary tract symptoms despite proteinuria
sports activity before musculoskeletal symptom onset

evidence_items.source_text: Since they were young, the two brothers’ mother noticed small black spots on their underpants and bed sheets that wouldn’t disappear even after washing. This phenomenon continued until they received a diagnosis.

In their early 40s, pigmentation of the sclera began to appear in both brothers, along with pigmentation of the ears and fingers. The patient was examined at an ophthalmology department, but no underlying cause for the discolouration could be concluded, and further investigations were not initiated.

When the patient was in his late 40s, he began regular monitoring for chronic cough, during which eosinophils were detected in blood samples. The initial lung function test revealed a result of 60%, raising suspicion of eosinophilic asthma.

In his early 50s, the patient was incidentally found to have proteinuria during a routine check by his general practitioner, despite never experiencing urinary tract symptoms. This led to an extended examination of the kidneys (see timeline below) due to differential diagnoses such as renal cancer, glomerulonephritis, diabetic kidney failure and myelomatosis. The patient’s renal function and proteinuria were regularly monitored at a nephrology department, and medication for hypertension (losartan) was attempted as a treatment to decrease the proteinuria.

Regarding musculoskeletal symptoms, he first sought medical attention for knee problems in his 50s. Before this, the patient had been very active and played football and handball at competitive levels. Initially, the musculoskeletal symptoms were thought to be related to this active lifestyle. Subsequently, many years passed with musculoskeletal symptoms progressing from knee problems to include diffuse lower back pain and eventually extending to encompass pain in the groin and hips.

The patient himself directed medical attention toward the possibility of alkaptonuria. The revelation came about due to the parallel experience of diffuse musculoskeletal pain by both him and his twin brother. Subsequently, the twin brother was scheduled for a surgical procedure. During the operation, surgeons encountered bone tissue with black discolouration, prompting the termination of the procedure.

The diagnosis was conclusively established through a diagnostic triad, including a urine spot test for HGA in both brothers and genetic DNA testing of the twin brother. This unveiled a heterozygous pathogenic variant in the two genes c.481G>A, p.(Gly161Arg) and c.1017G>T, p.(Met339Ile).
The spinal cysts identified in the corpus of Th9 and Th10 on high-resolution CT.
The distinctive black discolouration observed on the femur head during the total hip arthroplasty.
